title: The three left behind
hookLine: three men who stayed from Tabuk are forgiven after long waiting because they told the truth (9:118)
carry: the earth felt narrow, then wide

cards: Dawn, in Medina. A man is praying the morning prayer on the roof of his house, alone. For fifty nights, no one in the city has spoken to him.
Then, from the top of a hill called Sal', a voice shouts as loud as it can: Ka'b ibn Malik, good news! He falls down in prostration.
You met Ka'b last year, the day he told the Prophet ﷺ the plain truth: he had no excuse for staying home from Tabuk. Today, the verse that ended his waiting, and the waiting from the inside.

teach.h: A KING'S LETTER, INTO THE OVEN.
teach.b: Ka'b tells the waiting himself, in Bukhari and Muslim. His two companions in it, Murara and Hilal, stayed home and wept. Ka'b, the youngest, kept going out.
He prayed in the mosque, greeted the Prophet, and watched to see if his lips moved in reply.

Then a letter came from the north, from the king of Ghassan: we hear your master has shunned you; come to us, and we'll honor you. Ka'b read it and said: this too is a test. And he threw it into an oven.
Then verse one hundred eighteen came down.

In paraphrase: God turned also to the three who were left behind, when the earth, vast as it is, became narrow for them, and their own souls became narrow, and they knew there was no refuge from God except in Him.
Then He turned to them, so that they could turn.

teach.h: GOD TURNS FIRST; THEN THEY TURN.
teach.b: Notice the order: God turns first; then they turn.
The verse before, one hundred seventeen, says God had already turned to the Prophet and to those who marched with him in the hour of hardship, after some of their hearts had nearly swerved.
So the three aren't the only ones who needed mercy; they share a sentence with everyone who went.
Verse one hundred nineteen closes it: be with the truthful.

teach.h: THE EARTH FELT NARROW, THEN WIDE.
teach.b: When Ka'b came to the Prophet that morning, it was the Prophet's face that shone with joy. Ka'b offered to give away all his wealth; he was told to keep some.
And he vowed that, since the truth had saved him, he would speak only the truth for the rest of his life.

how: The story of Ka'b ibn Malik is taught at length in Muslim study circles as a lesson in honesty and repentance, and 9:118–119 are recited as a reminder that God turns toward people so that they can turn back, and to be with the truthful.

God turned first to the Prophet and those who marched, some of whose hearts had nearly swerved.
in 9:118, God turns to them so that they can turn
the order matters: God turns first, then they turn back.
Ka'b accepted the king's invitation while he waited

games.q: you're Ka'b, shunned for weeks. a foreign king writes: come to us, and we'll honor you. what do you do?
o: go; anything is better than this silence.
write back and ask for time.
call it a test, and throw the letter in the oven.
games.why: he burned it. days later the verse came, and the good news was shouted from the hill of Sal'.

practice: Bring to mind something you got wrong where you're still waiting for someone to answer, soften or trust you again. Notice the narrowness, and any easy way out, a story that makes it not your fault; leave that one in the oven.
If you pray, turn toward God with it, the way the three did, with nowhere else to go.

wordCard.voice: Ka'b. One of the three left behind, who told the truth about Tabuk, waited fifty nights, and was turned to by God in 9:118. Today's word.
